newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE coffee retreats in late sell-off on NY.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE coffee retreats in late sell-off on NY.

text.p: LIFFE robusta coffee futures succumbed to a late sell-off after hefty New York losses to finish Thursday sharply lower in fairly volatile trade, traders said.
"London was just following down," said one. "Also, there was not much industry support underneath."
By the close, most-active September stood $54 down at $1,771 per tonne after hitting the session's floor at $1,757, a 3.7 percent loss on the day and just $2 above its key support.
The day's peak was $1,850, seen as the immediate chart hurdle.
Other traded months lost between $19 and $65.
The market had started off higher in line with expectation and stayed firmer into the midday close after another good showing in New York the day earlier.
But the uptrend proved shortlived and London started to come off in the afternoon, dragged down by a reversal in the arabica futures on spec sell-off.
New York came under some fund selling after the market triggered major sell-stop new 173 U.S. cents a lb basis September. Origin selling was also seen.

Sentiment was dented by a build in certified stocks, continued mild winter weather in Brazil's coffee belt and a restatement by the U.S. Department of Agriculture (USDA) of a 28 million Brazil 1997/98 coffee crop.
But traders said the fund selling in New York appeared to have ease with September seen stabilising at just above 162 level.

The USDA said on Wednesday it had confidence in its 28-million bag estimate of Brazil's 1997/98 coffee harvest, and that a lower estimate of 24 million by a U.S. agricultural attache did not take into account all factors influencing the crop.
"We stand by our numbers and the integrity of our system," said Ed Cissel, director of production estimates and crop assessment for the USDA's Foreign Agricultural Service.

The Association of Coffee Producing Countries had expressed concern about a four-million bag difference in a pair of recent crop estimates and sought an explanation from the USDA regarding the conflicting figures.
Futures volume was 6,013 lots. Options reached 962 lots.
